perspective:
Available to Gloria Bangura:

- She is Gloria Bangura, an administrative assistant at a large event planning company.
- Donald Ortega is her colleague, a part-time bartender during company events.
- Their relationship is professional but not personally close; they mostly interact during events.
- At a company event, she observed Donald’s lack of enthusiasm while serving drinks and had noticed his distracted demeanor over several events.
- She approached Donald and asked if he was okay with his job. He told her: “I guess I’m just not as into it as I used to be. It’s kind of repetitive, you know?”
- After reflecting, she suspected his job dissatisfaction might be tied to larger personal issues.
- She suggested he consider talking to a professional. Donald told her: “I haven’t really considered that, Gloria. I’m not sure if that would help.”
- She sensed a change in Donald’s behavior toward her afterward and worried he resented her suggestion as an overstep.
- She apologized, explaining she only wanted to help because she cared and didn’t mean to overstep or make assumptions.
- Donald told her: “It’s okay, Gloria. I was a bit taken aback at first, but I know you meant well. It’s just a lot to process.”
- She felt relieved that the apology was well-received and tension had eased.
- She invited Donald to collaborate on a new project, telling him she thought it could use his creative input. Donald accepted and said he appreciated it and wanted to be more involved.
- After the project, she observed Donald’s significant contributions and renewed enthusiasm.
- She believed he was a valuable team member and publicly acknowledged his work in a team meeting, praising his efforts as crucial to the project’s success.
- Donald responded: “Thank you, Gloria. That means a lot to me. I’m glad I could contribute and it feels great to be appreciated.”
